title: Fix build with BUILD_LAZY_TS_BACKEND=0
body:
## Author Notes

Found out while working on https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/188285 and seeing what can be disabled in default builds. Pretty minimal.

## Agent Notes

When `BUILD_LAZY_TS_BACKEND=0`, the TS backend source files (including `ts_backend_impl.cpp` defining `InitTorchScriptBackend`) are excluded from libtorch at the CMake level. However, `torch/csrc/lazy/python/init.cpp` still referenced these symbols unconditionally — the existing guards only checked `FBCODE_CAFFE2`/`OVRSOURCE`, not `BUILD_LAZY_TS_BACKEND`. Since `BUILD_LAZY_TS_BACKEND` was never exposed as a C++ preprocessor define, the code had no way to know the backend was absent, resulting in an undefined symbol error at import time.

The fix adds `BUILD_LAZY_TS_BACKEND` as a compile definition on the `torch_python` CMake target (following the same pattern as `USE_NUMPY` and `USE_CUFILE`), and gates all TS-backend-specific code in `init.cpp` on it.

Authored with the help of an AI assistant (Claude Code).
